title: Omniglass Lab Device Profile
description: Schema for simulator device profile YAMLs in internal/sim/profiles/devices/. A profile defines a device type the simulator can serve: its identity, protocol surfaces, autonomous behaviors, computed fields, and default state.

name.description: Stable identifier for this profile. Used as the cross-reference key from system profiles and as the lookup key in the in-memory profile store. Lowercase, hyphenated.

manufacturer.description: Display-only manufacturer name. Surfaces in device pages, inventory exports, and the doc fixture.

model.description: Display-only model identifier. Surfaces in device pages and inventory.

device_type.description: Coarse category used by inventory/grouping. Convention: 'video-codec', 'display', 'dsp', 'touch-panel', 'control-processor', 'switcher', etc. Free-form but kebab-case.

slug_prefix.description: Hostname prefix used when generating device hostnames in a fleet. Short and unique enough that the eventual hostname is readable.

interfaces.description: Protocol surfaces this device exposes, each served on the device's own loopback address.

behaviors.description: Autonomous, scheduled mutations applied to the device's state at runtime, temperature drift, scheduled state changes. Each behavior runs a goroutine and emits a StateChange event per tick. For monotonic time counters (uptime) use computed instead, which is resolved on read and emits no events.

computed.description: Read-derived fields, computed on every read rather than written by a timer. Unlike behaviors, computed fields run no goroutine and emit no StateChange event. The canonical use is uptime as elapsed-since-boot.

overrides.description: State field overrides used by reduced or variant configurations.

defaults.description: Free-form state tree the device boots with. Paths referenced by routes/commands/oid_map should have a declared default here.

doc_fixture.description: Optional documentation fixture rendered into the device's playground. Free-form.

extends.description: Another device profile whose surface this one carries and adds to (a control processor answers everything its touch panel does). The base's interfaces come first; one named again here keeps its protocol and port and gains this profile's routes, commands, subjects and OIDs; behaviors and computed fields append; defaults deep-merge, this profile's winning.

products.description: Other products this profile simulates: variants of the same kind of device (the same component type) on the same driver. Each may overlay the profile's defaults with its own identity.

name.description: The product's name in the product catalog.

defaults.description: Deep-merged over the profile's defaults for this product.

doc.description: Human-readable documentation metadata. Surfaces in device pages and the playground.

name.description: Operator-facing identifier for this interface (e.g. 'web-admin', 'cli-ssh', 'snmp'). Used as the human handle in routes/commands documentation.

protocol.description: Wire protocol.  icmp is answered by the kernel, so it declares reachability without a listener; websocket serves a JSON control socket (see websocket).

tls_validity_days.description: A tls face's certificate validity window in days, counted from the face's start; 0 (the default) is a year.  Only on a face with tls.

loss_pct.description: The share of datagrams a udp face drops, in percent, each way, seeded from the device and the face so a run's losses repeat. Only on a udp face.

events.description: An http face's server-sent events stream: every change to the declared state paths, one numbered event each, replayed from a reconnect's Last-Event-ID, behind the face's auth.

retry_ms.description: The reconnection time the stream asks for, in milliseconds; zero asks none.

paths.description: The state paths whose changes it streams, each with everything beneath it; none streams every change.

drop_path.description: The path the console fires (POST) to drop every stream, as a restart would.

websocket.description: A websocket face's control socket: a JSON message per text frame. A subscribe is acknowledged and then pushes every change to its paths; a get or a set is answered by a result carrying the request's id, after any push it causes. Behind the face's own auth (basic, header, bearer or query).

path.description: The path the upgrade is served at.

paths.description: The state paths a subscriber may watch and a get may read, each with everything beneath it; none is every path.

settable.description: The state paths a set may write.

drop_path.description: The path the console fires (POST) to drop every socket, as a restart would.

api_surface.description: Logical surface name shared with sibling interfaces that route to the same response set.

oid_map.description: Map of state-tree paths (e.g. 'status.device.power') to SNMP OIDs.  Each entry answers SNMP GET and GETNEXT from live state.

mib.description: SNMP MIB filename that defines this device's enterprise OID arc. Set on snmp interfaces with an enterprise MIB.

refused_community.description: A community an snmp face knows and refuses: answered with authorizationError, where any community but its own is dropped silently. Only on an snmp face.

query.description: The query parameter a query-auth http face reads its api key from; apikey when empty.

login_path.description: A form or token http face's login path: /login (form) and /api/login (token) when empty.

session_ttl.description: The seconds a session a form or token face opens lives: a token's expires_in (an hour when zero), and a form session until it is expired when zero.

algorithm.description: A digest http face's hash: MD5 when empty.

expire_path.description: The path the console fires (POST) to expire every session a form or token face opened and rotate a digest face's nonce, as a reboot would.

interval.description: Go duration string ('10s', '500ms', '5m'). Required for phase 1 behaviors.

emit.description: Optional outbound webhook the behavior POSTs each tick (after mutations apply). The device's only egress-HTTP capability: best-effort, short-timeout, log-and-continue on failure. url and body are templates rendered against the tick context (.State, .Defaults, .Hostname, .DeviceID, .IP). An empty rendered url disables emission (configured-off); the behavior still ticks. Method is always POST with Content-Type application/json.

url.description: Target URL template. Typically a single profile-level config value, e.g. '{{ .Defaults.configuration.webhook.target_url }}', so an operator points every device instance at the collector with one edit. Empty render = emission disabled.

body.description: POST body template (sent as application/json). May interpolate post-mutation state, e.g. '{"host":"{{ .Hostname }}","event":"meeting.started","ts":{{ now }}}'.

path.description: State path readers observe (e.g. 'status.device.uptime'). Resolved on every read; must not also be written by a behavior.

kind.description: elapsed: integer seconds since the 'since' anchor timestamp.

since.description: Anchor state path holding a Unix-epoch seconds value (e.g. 'status.device.boot_epoch'). Seeded at device start; re-set to '{{ now }}' on reboot.
